title: African Development Bank — WATAF Strengthening Tax Administration Capacity Project in West Africa (STACP-WA), 2026
description:
Verbatim from the source:

> Liberia is among six West African countries set to benefit from a US$5.3 million African Development Bank (AfDB)-financed initiative designed to strengthen tax administration, improve domestic revenue mobilization, and build resilient revenue systems across the region.
>
> The four-year Strengthening Tax Administration Capacity Project in West Africa (STACP-WA) was officially launched by the West African Tax Administration Forum (WATAF) on Tuesday, August 18.
>
> The initiative is financed through a UA4 million grant from the African Development Fund/Transition Support Facility Pillar III, equivalent to approximately US$5.3 million. It will benefit Burkina Faso, The Gambia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Liberia, and Sierra Leone.
>
> Bangura said the project will help beneficiary countries improve domestic, trade, and extractive-sector tax administration, strengthen compliance, and reduce revenue leakages.
>
> It will also support digital tax tools, VAT and e-invoicing reforms, taxpayer education, gender-responsive tax systems, and improved governance of natural resource revenues.
>
> According to Bangura, the project has three main components: strengthening the efficient administration of domestic and trade taxes; improving natural resource revenues in resource-rich countries; and supporting project management, coordination, and institutional capacity development within the WATAF Secretariat.
original_amount: UA 4 million (African Development Fund unit of account)

title: Multinational - Strengthening Health Systems and Medical Regulations (SHyMeR) Project
description: The Strengthening Health Systems and Medical Regulations Project (SHyMeR) is a multinational regional public goods operation designed to strengthen health-system resilience and medical-product regulation in seven eligible African Development Fund countries in the ECOWAS region: Benin, The Gambia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Liberia, Sierra Leone and Togo. The project will strengthen National Medicines Regulatory Authorities and laboratories, improve access to safe and quality-assured medical and nutrition products, enhance diagnostic and emergency-response capacities, and build the skills of the regional health workforce. It will support the regulatory authorities of Benin, The Gambia, Liberia and Sierra Leone in progressing towards World Health Organization Maturity Level 3; equip The Gambia’s national quality-control laboratory; establish cross-border One Health laboratories in Benin and Togo; and repair, maintain and equip biomedical, diagnostic, intensive-care and cancer-diagnostic facilities in Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Liberia and Sierra Leone. The project will also develop an integrated regional health data hub and electronic medical-record systems, introduce digital learning and virtual or augmented-reality simulation laboratories in three universities, train health professionals and biomedical technicians, and support youth-led biomedical and digital-health enterprises. At the regional level, it will promote harmonized health policies, pooled procurement of essential medicines, sustainable health financing, climate-resilient health investment planning, and the integration of One Health, nutrition and gender-based violence considerations into community-health policies. The total project cost is estimated at UA 11.435 million, equivalent to approximately USD 15.712 million. It will be financed by an African Development Fund Regional Public Goods grant of UA 10.380 million, or about USD 14.262 million, and a cash counterpart contribution from ECOWAS/WAHO of UA 1.055 million, or approximately USD 1.450 million. The grant recipient and executing agency is the West African Health Organization (WAHO). The project development objective is to enhance resilience in West Africa by strengthening health systems and medical regulations to support the provision of quality routine health services and effective responses to public-health and nutrition emergencies in seven eligible ECOWAS member states. title: Multinational - Designing, mainstreaming and capacity building for gender equity in regulatory frameworks
description: This project concerns designing, mainstreaming, and capacity building for gender-equity in regulatory frameworks. West African Monetary Agency (WAMA)’s project focuses on conducting a gender analysis that will inform the design of gender sensitive policy and regulatory framework reviews. WAMA intends to work with ADFI on mainstreaming gender within the core digital financial services (DFS) regulatory frameworks of the ECOWAS countries/region. To do this, WAMA has singled out the ongoing Regional Payments Framework Gateway as a strategic start to the project that will present an opportunity to execute gender gap analysis in their i) financial inclusion strategy; ii) data analytics strategy for gender disaggregated data; iii) digital payment services such as microloans; iv) digital identity; and v) digital payments infrastructure. WAMA’s business model is to work via the Council of Governors (Heads of Central Banks of the ECOWAS region). Once policy and regulatory revisions are ready, they will be tabled to the Council of Governors, who in turn work with the Council of Ministers. Upon endorsement from Council of Ministers, the revised policies and regulations are shared with Heads of States for review and approval. The expected outputs are: i) detailed implementation plan for the revised policies; ii) gender indicators developed to guide gap analysis; and iii) gender score card developed to track progress. The purpose of the project is to design gender-sensitive DFS regulatory standards in ECOWAS region and the adoption of gender-friendly DFS regulatory frameworks at national and regional levels. The direct beneficiaries are financially excluded women in ECOWAS, the majority of whom are informal traders and an estimated 64% living below poverty line, compared to 68% of the overall population living below poverty line. Indirect beneficiaries are households that rely on women for sustenance, DFS service providers targeting women, government entities across ECOWAS working to address gender disparities in the DFS sector, NGOs and institutions working to improve women’s access to capital, and hence access to DFS services.

title: Maroc Telecom West Africa Submarine Fibre Optic Cable - \u20ac150M Investment
description: Maroc Telecom invested €150 million ($157 million) in the construction of the West Africa submarine fibre optic cable, a 9,414 km system connecting the group's Moov Africa SSA subsidiaries to the international network via Morocco. The cable has 8 landing points across 7 countries including Côte d'Ivoire (Abidjan), Togo (Lomé), Benin (Cotonou), Gabon (Libreville), Mauritania (Nouadhibou), Morocco (Casablanca, Dakhla), and Portugal (Lisbon). South segment operational July 2021; North segment operational April 2022. Capacity: 20-60 Tbps. Financed by a consortium of Maroc Telecom and its African subsidiaries.
